title: Simamaung Cares for NTT Earthquake Survivors: Delivering Clean Water, Supplementary Food, and Psychosocial Services in Nagekeo
excerpt: Simamaung, through Relawan Nusantara, delivered clean water, PMT (supplementary feeding) packages, and psychosocial services to residents affected by the earthquake in NTT (East Nusa Tenggara) in Marapokot Village, Nagekeo.
seoTitle: Simamaung Delivers Aid After NTT Earthquake - Relawan Nusantara
seoDescription: Simamaung, through Relawan Nusantara, delivers clean water, supplementary food, and psychosocial services after the NTT earthquake in Marapokot, Nagekeo.
html:
More than a month after an earthquake shook Flores on 15 August 2026, communities in a number of affected areas are still going through the recovery process. In Marapokot Village, Aesesa District, Nagekeo Regency, some residents are still staying at self-organized evacuation points around their settlements.

Under these conditions, basic needs remain a constant concern, from the availability of clean water for families to the nutritional needs of children who are still growing and developing amid the post-disaster situation.

Seeing these needs, Simamaung and all Maungers delivered a holistic aid program through Relawan Nusantara, covering the distribution of 20,000 liters of clean water, 30 packages of Pemberian Makanan Tambahan (PMT, supplementary feeding), and psychosocial support activities for affected communities in Nagekeo Regency.

20,000 Liters of Clean Water for Survivors' Needs

For residents still living in self-organized evacuation tents, clean water is a need that cannot wait. Water is used for all kinds of daily needs, from drinking and cooking to keeping themselves and their surroundings clean.

A total of 20,000 liters of clean water was distributed to help meet the needs of people at a number of self-organized evacuation points.

The aid reached families who are still adapting to life in temporary shelter. In the midst of recovery, the availability of water is one of the essentials that allows daily activities to carry on.

For families affected by disaster, having water available is not only about meeting today's needs. There are household chores that still need to be done, meals that must be prepared, and family hygiene that must be maintained.

Meeting Children's Nutritional Needs Through 30 PMT Packages

Beyond the need for clean water, attention was also given to the children of Marapokot through the distribution of 30 supplementary feeding (PMT) packages.

Meeting children's nutritional intake is an important part of a post-disaster situation. While family life is still in the recovery stage, children's nutritional needs must still be looked after so that they can grow and stay active.

However, the activities with the children of Marapokot did not stop at handing out food.

After the PMT distribution, the children were invited to play football together. A simple field became a space for them to run, chase the ball, joke, and laugh together.

For a few moments, an atmosphere usually colored by post-disaster conditions gave way to the lively sound of children.

Psychosocial Support Through Football

Post-disaster recovery focuses not only on physical needs and logistics, but also on the mental health of residents, especially children. For this reason, Simamaung Media, through Relawan Nusantara, provided psychosocial services in an interactive format.

The volunteers held a football session with affected children on a simple local field. Through the game, jokes, and laughter, the volunteers created a safe space for the children to release their trauma and regain the joy of childhood.

More Than Aid, This Is About Accompanying Recovery

For children, the chance to play may seem simple. But in a post-disaster situation, space to play and interact with their peers is an important part of their daily lives.

The same is true of clean water and food. Both are needs that are part of everyday life, yet they mean a great deal to families going through a period of recovery.

For that reason, the aid in Marapokot is not seen only as the distribution of basic necessities. There is an effort to accompany the community through the days after the disaster, including making sure children continue to receive attention and have space to enjoy their childhood.

Recovery does not always happen in big steps. Sometimes it begins with simple things: water available for the family, enough food for a child, or the chance for them to play and smile again.

Thank you, Simamaung and all Maungers, for the trust and care you have entrusted through Relawan Nusantara. Through this support, we hope to help ease the needs of the community in Marapokot, Nagekeo Regency, while the post-earthquake recovery process is still under way.

Because rebuilding life after a disaster is not only about repairing what was damaged, but also about making sure basic needs continue to be met and children still have the chance to grow, play, and look ahead to better days. Let us help NTT (East Nusa Tenggara) recover now!

Luaskan Manfaat
